text.p: Italian debt markets took the brunt of investor jitters in another negative session, with futures shedding nearly a point by late trade.

Comments from Germany's Ifo economic research institute and Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing both combined to feed growing concerns about the strength of the dollar and what it might do to European interest rates.

Ifo said European central banks were coming under pressure to raise interest rates to support their currencies while Issing said the German central bank was concerned about the pace of the mark's decline against the U.S. currency.
"There is something happening," said one broker, referring to a change in sentiment on prospects for German interest rates. "People feel change on monetary policy in Germany is possible."
The July 2007 Btp was 49 basis points down at 100.70, with the yield 6.69 pct and the spread over Bunds 99 bps -- squeaking under the 100 level. Sept LIFFE futures fell 92 bps to 134.98.

The broker said Btps were suffering not only because of the streak of gains in the last month without a real pullback, but also because, if German rates were to go higher, this could create potential problems for meeting Maastricht treaty criteria on EMU, which revives concerns the project may be delayed.
Italy, perceived as unlikely to sustain its efforts for fiscal virtue without the carrot of EMU membership, tends to suffer when delay concerns unnerve the market.

At home, inflation rose a shade to 1.6 percent year on year in July after 1.4 percent in June, although the gain was due to statistical factors. The dollar is causing some talk however that lira prices may rise and push up inflation levels.
On trade activity, dealers had been busy with selling coming from all round and volumes healthy -- which they said was a bearish signal when the market was heading down.
